paper.title: Adaptive Experimental Design for Policy Learning

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual fixed-budget BAI / adaptive experimental design for policy learning (location-shift bandit model)
unmapped: recommendation is a policy chosen from an exogenously given policy class Pi with Natarajan dimension M; regret is measured against the best policy in Pi
conditional variances sigma^a(x)^2 are fixed (location-shift model) and unknown to the learner; context distribution zeta unknown
settings.definition_quote:
Let $(\sigma^a)^2 \colon \mathcal{X} \to (0, +\infty)$ be a function that is exogenously given but \emph{unknown} to the decision-maker. Let $\zeta$ be a distribution of $X$ that is exogenously given but \emph{unknown} to the decision-maker, which is supported on $\mathcal{X}$. 
Then, a \emph{location-shift bandit model} $\mathcal{P}$ is defined as follows:
\begin{align}
    &\mathcal{P} \coloneqq \mathcal{P}_\zeta \coloneqq \Big\{P \in \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{Y}^K \times \mathcal{X})
    \colon
    \forall a \in [K]\ \ \ \forall x \in \mathcal{X},\ \ \ \mathrm{Var}_P(Y^a \mid X=x) = \sigma^a(x), \\
    &\ Y^a - \mu^a(P)(x)\ \mathrm{is}\ \mathrm{zeo}\mathchar`-\mathrm{mean}\ \mathrm{subgaussian}\ \mathrm{given}\ x,\ \ \ \mu^a(P)(x) \in (-\infty, +\infty),\ \ \ \mathrm{marg}_{\mathcal{X}}(P) = \zeta
    \Big\},
\end{align}

symbols.M: Natarajan dimension d_N(Pi) of the policy class
symbols.V_X: E_{X~zeta}[sqrt(sum_a sigma^a(X)^2)], expected root of summed conditional variances

conditions: there exists a context distribution zeta (uniform on M shattered points) for which the bound holds
worst case over P in the location-shift model P_zeta (Gaussian submodel)

source.label: thm:null_lower_bound
source.quote: There exists a distribution $\zeta$ on $\mathcal{X}$ such that for any $K \geq 2$, any null consistent strategy $\pi$ with a policy class $\Pi$ such that $d_{\mathrm{N}}(\Pi) = M$ satisfies $\sup_{P\in\mathcal{P}_\zeta} \sqrt{T}\mathbb{E}_P[R(P)(\pi)] \geq \frac{1}{8}\mathbb{E}_{X \sim \zeta}[\sqrt{M\sum_{a\in[K]}(\sigma^a(X))^2}] + o(1)$ as $T\to\infty$

results.notes: Worst-case (minimax over P) asymptotic bound; divided by sqrt(T). Variance-dependent, so marked instance_dependent in terms of variances though it is minimax over means.

symbols.M: VC dimension d_VC(Pi) of the policy class

conditions: there exists a context distribution zeta for which the bound holds

source.label: thm:null_lower_bound_ref
source.quote: There exists a distribution $\zeta$ on $\mathcal{X}$ such that for $K = 2$, any null consistent strategy $\pi$ with policy class $\Pi$ such that $d_{\mathrm{VC}}(\Pi) = M$ satisfies $\sup_{P\in\mathcal{P}_\zeta} \sqrt{T}\mathbb{E}_P[R(P)(\pi)] \geq \frac{1}{8}\mathbb{E}_{X \sim \zeta}[\sqrt{M(\sigma^{1}(X) + \sigma^{2}(X))^2}] + o(1)$ as $T\to\infty$.

symbols.kappa: entropy integral kappa(Pi) of the policy class; kappa <= C*sqrt(log(d)*d_N(Pi)) for K>=3

conditions: Assumption 5.1: estimators of w* and mu^a converge uniformly almost surely
Assumption 5.3 (used in proof): Hamming covering number N_H(eps,Pi) <= C exp(D (1/eps)^omega), 0<omega<0.5
Lemma C.1 (clipping with U_T = T^alpha asymptotically negligible; proof omitted)
holds for any zeta and any P in P_zeta

source.label: thm:regret_upper_bound
source.quote: Suppose that Assumption~\ref{asm:consistent} holds. Then, for any $\zeta$ and any $P\in\mathcal{P}_\zeta$, the expected simple regret of the PLAS strategy satisfies $\sqrt{T}\mathbb{E}_P[R(P)(\widehat{\pi}^{\mathrm{PLAS}}_T)] \leq (108.8 \kappa(\Pi) + 870.4)\mathbb{E}_{X \sim \zeta}[\sqrt{\sum^K_{a=1}(\sigma^a(X))^2}] + o(1)$ if $K \geq 3$ ...

results.notes: Pointwise in P (not stated uniformly). Proof relies on loose arguments and Assumption 5.3 not mentioned in theorem.

symbols.kappa: entropy integral kappa(Pi); kappa <= 2.5*sqrt(d_N(Pi)) for K=2

conditions: Assumption 5.1: estimators of w* and mu^a converge uniformly almost surely
Assumption 5.3 (used in proof): Hamming covering number bound
results.notes: With kappa <= 2.5 sqrt(M) gives (272 sqrt(M)+870.4) factor as remarked in paper.
